html:
The Kabwe skull, also called Broken Hill Man, is the skull of an early human found by a miner at the Broken Hill lead and zinc mine, now Kabwe in Zambia, in 1921.

It was the first fossil of an early human found in Africa, three years before the Taung Child. Scientists now place it in the species Homo heidelbergensis or a close relative, and dating published in 2020 put it at about 300,000 years old, so its kind lived at the same time as the first Homo sapiens and Homo naledi.

The skull was taken to the Natural History Museum in London, where it remains. Zambia has asked for its return as part of its national heritage.
sum: The Kabwe skull, also called Broken Hill Man, is the skull of an early human found by a miner at the Broken Hill lead and zinc mine, now Kabwe in Zambia, in 1921.
